_comment: What the hands-on moments say: shown on screen and spoken by the narrator (scripts/narrate.py voices each line to media/audio/labs/<key>.mp3). Facts come from the cited story beats; comparisons (car, train, jet, sound) are everyday figures.
laser-back: It's back! The light took about two and a half seconds to reach the Moon and return. Light travels about 300,000 km every second, so the Moon is about 384,400 km away.
laser-great: Great timing! You stopped the clock right as the light came home.
laser-close: Nice try! Real telescopes time it to a tiny fraction of a second. Fire again to get closer.
laser-nostop: Fire again, and this time stop the clock just as the light comes back.
wheel-start: The pink wheel can't turn, so it drags and digs a trench. Keep driving!
wheel-found: Bright white soil! When Spirit really did this in 2007, its instruments found the soil was about 90% pure silica. On Earth, silica like this forms in hot springs or steam vents. Keep driving to the end of the track.
wheel-parked: You made it to the end of the track. That's the whole drive! Press Start again to drive it once more.
ion-start: Hold it down longer: something happens soon!
ion-car: 100 km/h faster: as fast as a car! Keep holding.
ion-train: 300 km/h faster: a high-speed train! Keep going.
ion-jet: 900 km/h faster: a passenger jet! One more to go.
ion-sound: 1,235 km/h faster: faster than the speed of sound! That's the end of our test. Dawn kept up its gentle push for a very long time, and that's how it reached Vesta and then Ceres. Press Reset to fly again.
